newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bank stocks roar up on shake-up speculation.
newsitem.headline: French bank stocks roar up on shake-up speculation.

text.p: French bank shares roared ahead in heavy trading on Wednesday as speculation on takeovers and wider bank stock upgrades intensified in the wake of Deutsche Bank's declaration that it could make an acquisition in France.

Shares in Credit Commercial de France and Banque Nationale de Paris soared by more than 10 percent to new year highs in brisk morning business, triggering a brief trading suspension in both stocks for a cooling-off period.
Other bank stocks also surged by well over the advance in the CAC-40 leading share index, which itself hit an all-time high of 3,010,85 points, about three percent up, before midday.

Traders and analysts said a major bank merger in Germany had already rekindled speculation on further bank restructuring in France on Tuesday and that Deutsche Bank's comments on Wednesday had added fuel to the flames.

Some of the big gainers including leaders BNP and Societe Generale were improbable takeover targets but were benefitting from a view that the time was ripe for a fresh upgrade of long-lagging French bank stocks, they said.

CCF, whose shares were up 12.08 percent at 293.1 francs at 1214 GMT after hitting a year high of 300.0 francs earlier, is seen as the smallest of the leading banks and a possible target along with Credit National, they said.

Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken-und Weschel-Bank AG said on Monday they planned to merge and Deutsche Bank chief executive Rolf Breuer said on Wednesday his group was considering a French bank buy.
"It's a speculative climate and the market just exploded after Brueur's declarations," said Romain Burnand, bank analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.
"Liquidity's heavy and investors are looking for ideas...but there's also the catch-up on other European banks. French banks have underperformed for a year now."

"I don't think Deutsche Bank would be foolish enough to announce a takeover bid for a French bank. I'd say it is more likely that it is in the process of positioning itself vis-a-vis Credit Lyonnais or CIC," he said.

CIC, or Credit Industriel et Commercial, is a privatisation candidate and state bank Credit Lyonnais could be in the longer term -- although the position on both banks is still unclear following the return to power of a Socialist-led government on June 1.
A French equities trader in London said he shared the view that BNP or SocGen were unlikely takeover targets.

CCF or other smaller banks like Credit National could come into play alongside sale candidates CIC and Credit Lyonnais, although speculation at this stage was based more on general optimism than specifics, he said.

"It's the outside element coming into play. There's what happened in the last three or four days in Germany and today there's Deutsche saying it would be looking to buy something in France," said the trader.

"Starting from there the whole banking sector has to be reevaluated. CCF is a likely target. I don't think BNP or SocGen could be targets, for political reasons as well as everything else, but they are gaining because the whole sector has to be reevaluated."
BNP shares were up 10.74 percent at 1209 GMT at 276.4 francs after hitting a year high of 282.0.
Societe Generale shares were up 8.4 percent at 800 francs, while those of Paribas were up 7.36 percent at 432.0 francs and Credit National shares were 4.22 percent higher at 373.0 francs.
Credit Lyonnais investment certificates, which are like shares without voting rights, were up 4.96 percent at 324.0 francs.
